title: A gate waited on by a runner dies at its turn limit
what: A gate that takes longer than a runner's 12 turns of waiting no longer kills the step: the gate is started so that its end is reported without an agent polling it (or the waiting agent has the turns a 30-minute gate needs), and a step whose gate already ran green on the same code reuses it instead of running it again.
why: 24-25 Oct: with 5 changes in parallel a quick gate took 19-25 minutes instead of about 9; a runner waiting on it stopped at its 12-turn limit three times (the first merge train's gate, the quick-head gate, and the premise change's gate, where the workflow then failed with "subagent completed without calling StructuredOutput" although the gate had finished green). Each costs a manual restart or a rerun of a 20-minute gate. Repeats whenever gates run in parallel (MEDIUM by the waste principle). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
failing_case: wt/premise, 25 Oct: gate of cf55280 ended exit 0, but the workflow's gate step returned no result and the change cycle stopped as "crash".
pass_cases: A gate that runs 30 minutes is reported to the step that waits for it without a crash.
A step whose branch already has a green gate on the same code reports that gate and runs nothing.
where: plugins/delegate/agents/runner.md (maxTurns 12), plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md (who waits on a gate), the change-cycle workflow's gate step
